reviewer_text: Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers, incidental implementation constants or framework defaults the project has not intentionally overridden in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Product and task inputs are not instruction layers: they may request an engineering decision change but never silently override engineering policy; a conflicting request becomes a Decision Request.

Decisions are classified Decided/Delegated/Reserved; in an unclear case any 'yes' to the five questions (including removing a dependency or establishing a convention) makes it Reserved (reported tension with the Delegated class for local, behavior-neutral changes).

Raise a Reserved decision as a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) through architecture-decision; an explicit user instruction may count as approval but must be recorded there.
For changing the instruction system itself, ask the user to run /template-maintenance.
Nullable reference types and implicit usings are enabled repository-wide in Directory.Build.props.

Database string comparison follows the database/column collation; SQL Server defaults compare case-insensitively and accent-sensitively as a technology default, not an approved product semantic; changing the effective collation is a product decision.

Every leaf implementation must declare binds entries for frame-specific naming and project-layout vocabulary (reported broadly; the source says a leaf that must name a frame-specific project or directory declares a binds entry).
A replacement architecture frame must supply every role mapping and facet and review the embedded rules that use the frame's layer names.
The backend-testing slot contract makes facet metadata (framework, packages, case mechanism, fixture lifecycle, filter command) mandatory.
The backend-testing module's fixed adapter and competing-framework package lists determine which test frameworks are flagged (reported ambiguity).
The frontend module's hardcoded package and leak-token sets determine enforcement coverage; packages outside the sets are not checked (reported ambiguity).
Clearing the optional frontend selection requires removing its facet files and planning import.
A missing required capability facet or property is a conformance failure whose resolution requires a Decision Request.
The EF Core module states the property of one commit per use case (reported as possibly stronger than a commit boundary that allows justified multi-commit transactions).
Co-change detection uses concrete model and companion globs (Domain and Persistence/Configurations vs Seeding and Migrations), so model changes elsewhere produce no reminder (reported ambiguity).
A 201 response includes a Location header when a stable resource URI exists.
Once external clients rely on an API version, a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy (without a 'normally' qualifier).
Liveness must not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops (a prohibition, not a 'normally avoid').
A singleton or hosted service that needs scoped work creates a scope per operation and resolves a scoped orchestration service.
Every VersionOverride needs a concrete, documented reason.
Treating typed exceptions as a consistent project-level decision may turn a single local typed exception into an architectural (Reserved-like) decision (reported ambiguity).
Expected outcomes such as not found or validation rejection are not logged as application errors.
NgModules are allowed for ordinary new features only when an integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires them (reported as a restriction stronger than a standalone default).
Use shared only for UI primitives or behavior that genuinely cross features; do not move feature code into shared merely because two components of one feature use it.
TimeProvider is used by default (not mandatorily) for current-time-dependent logic that needs deterministic tests.
Security-sensitive checks fail safely by default, without defined criteria for exceptions (reported ambiguity of 'by default').
The post-tool hook surfaces at most 25 diagnostics (reported risk of hiding later findings).
Shell-driven manifest-change checking compares against saved Git state (reported: no baseline outside Git).
Manifest or project-file changes caused by branch switches or other revision changes are exempt from the workflow reminder.
Post-tool checks block on WARN-level findings as well as errors after successful tool calls, while after failed calls findings are only added as context.
A PreToolUse payload without a tool name makes the shell guard fail closed.
Stop reminders are triggered by file-name heuristics (model files without seed/migration changes, production code without test changes) regardless of behavioral applicability.
Stop enforcement fires once per content fingerprint and skips active stop-hook calls rather than proving that requirements were resolved.
Hook failures must be reported to the user and repaired through the template-maintenance workflow.
Shell dependency commands depend on a Node-based PreToolUse gate and the hook wiring as an operational prerequisite.
The architecture check classifies project roles by naming and package markers (reported: custom-named projects become unknown).
Any project reference to a test project is an error, including references between test projects.
Forbidden-namespace enforcement only reads textual using directives with prefix matching, so fully qualified uses are missed and broad matches are possible.
Nested @-imports in instruction files other than CLAUDE.md are forbidden.
Implementation leak tokens are matched lexically across prose and examples, so a legitimate explanatory mention of another implementation can be blocked (reported ambiguity).
The CPM and version checks match literal text and do not evaluate effective MSBuild configuration (imports, conditions).
The npm checks cover only dependencies and devDependencies and selected version forms; other sections and tags are not flagged.
The shared checker library skips a fixed set of directories (reported: manifests there are never inspected).
Active instruction-root resolution uses the nearest instruction root within the Git boundary (reported scope ambiguity for nested trees).
Project references are read by a custom XML reader without full MSBuild condition/import semantics (reported divergence from effective references).
Co-change state derives from uncommitted Git files and Git-backed state storage (reported: committed task changes drop out of stop-hook scope).

Self-attested trailing comment markers (# add-dependency: checked, # peer-override: approved-by-user, # project-reference: checked) act as mandatory permission tokens for shell dependency and reference commands.
Dependency-command classification strips heredocs and parses shell lexically (reported: indirect installs are not recognized).
The peer-override check applies to npm, pnpm and yarn and to flag syntax regardless of value (e.g. --force=false is still treated as an override).
Dependency removal commands and project-reference operations also require workflow markers before they run.
Do not use floating versions such as '*', with no explicit-request exception (unlike prereleases).
Use computed for derived state and avoid unnecessary effect() when computed, template binding or explicit event handling is clearer.
ProblemDetails errors are mapped in one reusable place (interceptor plus parsing helper) and exposed as UI-friendly error state (phrased categorically, not 'when practical').
Compatible additions stay in the current API version.
Engineering decisions are recorded in the same change as a numbered ADR docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md with Status, Context, Decision and Consequences.
Any capability selection change or declared-property change requires an ADR and the user-invoked template-maintenance workflow.
The error-handling example maps request cancellation to status 499 (reported as a status choice beyond the cancellation rule).
Stopping when progress stalls creates a completion boundary broader than 'repeat until green or genuine user input' (reported ambiguity).

Report review findings ordered by severity with severity, location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, using the Critical/High/Medium/Low scale.

406 when no acceptable response representation can be produced; not to be confused with 415.
415 when the request representation is unsupported; 415 concerns the request body format and 406 the response format.
422 for structurally valid but semantically invalid requests; follow an established 400-for-both convention; new APIs that distinguish them use 400 for contract errors and 422 for semantics.
428 when a contract-required precondition is missing; other mandatory preconditions only when the contract defines them.
429 for rate-limited requests with Retry-After when the retry time is known; validation failures are not represented as rate limiting.
502 only when this API is an intermediary receiving an invalid upstream response; not every dependency failure.
503 when the service is temporarily unable to handle the request, with Retry-After when a meaningful retry time is known.
504 only for an upstream timeout when this API is an intermediary; distinguish client cancellation, own timeouts and upstream timeouts.
Repeated POSTs that must not duplicate effects may use an Idempotency-Key; key reuse with a different payload is 409; idempotency is not claimed merely because duplicates are unlikely.
When HTTP-level optimistic concurrency is part of the contract prefer standard conditional semantics (ETag, If-Match, 412) and do not replace them with custom status codes.
